title: Most Widely Cited Findings On LLM Behavior Fade Within 15 Months
summary:
Research into the stability of artificial intelligence claims shows that most results regarding how large language models behave lose their validity within 15 months of publication. The study re-tested 50 of the most widely cited behavioral findings—including those focusing on biases and hallucinations—to determine whether the original observations still held true.

The researchers found that the majority of the tested claims either no longer occurred or showed diminished effects over the 15 month period. The study suggests that findings on LLMs have a short shelf life, necessitating a regular review of AI knowledge as the models evolve.
